text.p: Singapore shares opened slightly stronger on Friday as blue chip buyers came back to the market following their steady departure on Thursday, dealers said.
"Yesterday we were quite weak because the blue chips tailed off, but they're coming back today," one local dealer said.
The market gave a muted response to a speech by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman, Alan Greenspan.
"The concensus is he will put rates up a quarter point in May. That view hasn't changed," one dealer said.
At 0215 GMT the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index was up 8.19 points at 2,067.57.
Market volume was a reasonable 76.9 million shares, with almost half concentrated on new listing Popular Holdings, which saw 35.6 million shares change hands on its debut day.
The stock opened at a 33 percent premium on its offer price of Singapore $0.36 before climbing to S$0.535 in the first few minutes and settling back to S$0.525 at 0215 GMT.
Early gainers were led by Creative Technology, up S$1.40 at S$27.60, easing back after earlier hitting a new high for the year of S$27.90.
Vickers Ballas led early losers, down S$1.24 at S$1.26 at 0215 GMT.
